minutes.summary: A three-member Public Access Cable Committee, down to a bare quorum with a new member just sworn in, opened its fiscal year by re-appointing its chair, vice chair and clerk/secretary, then heard the department manager's monthly report. The main substantive matter was that the committee's video-file storage system (NAS) had failed completely; the committee authorized purchase of a replacement from the maintenance budget line, discussed the Comcast cable contract renewal process, a planned studio relocation, new recordings of the trust fund commission and tri-board committee, and reviewed year-end financial and programming figures.

what_happened.line: The committee authorized a replacement video-storage system (NAS) after the old one failed entirely, funded from the maintenance line for an amount as heard on the recording.
The committee reorganized for the new fiscal year, appointing a chair, vice chair and clerk/secretary, though those votes are not audible in the recording.
The committee will start recording trust fund commission meetings and, from the next day, tri-board meetings of the select board, school committee and finance committee.
Studio relocation to the TCP/TC Pasios space is planned for mid-to-late July.
The next meeting was set for August 4th at 3:00pm as a schedule exception.

why_it_matters: Failure of the video-storage system put the archive of recorded public meetings at risk; the committee treated the fix as routine maintenance spending rather than a capital purchase, so it did not require a separate town vote.
Adding trust fund commission and tri-board meetings to the recording schedule would give residents video access to bodies not previously covered.
The Comcast cable contract, the studio move and FY27 budget prep were all discussed but not resolved, so residents following public access should expect more decisions on those at future meetings.
